# rustinion_monitor_template (Resource)

Manages a monitoring template: rules (Zabbix-style triggers such as last(vfs.fs.size[*,pused]) > {$VFS.FS.PUSED.MAX.CRIT}) evaluated on every device the template is linked to, one alert state per device, plus macro defaults and parent templates whose rules and macros it inherits. Built-in packs are read-only; reference them with the rustinion_monitor_template data source.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String)

### Optional

- `description` (String)
- `macro` (Block List) A user macro default, e.g. {$DISK_CRIT} = 90. Groups, devices and the organization can override it (rustinion_monitor_macro_override). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--macro))
- `parent_ids` (List of String) Templates (own or built-in) this one inherits rules and macro defaults from. Its own macro defaults beat its parents'.
- `rule` (Block List) A rule: func(item_key, window) comparator threshold. Rules keep their per-device state across updates as long as their name stays the same. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--rule))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.

<a id="nestedblock--macro"></a>
### Nested Schema for `macro`

Required:

- `macro` (String) Macro name in Zabbix syntax: {$NAME} with A-Z, 0-9, _ and .
- `value` (String)

Optional:

- `context` (String) Optional context, e.g. "/data" for {$VFS.FS.PUSED.MAX.CRIT:"/data"}.
- `description` (String)


<a id="nestedblock--rule"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rule`

Required:

- `comparator` (String)
- `item_key` (String) Item key, Zabbix syntax: system.cpu.util, vm.memory.utilization, vfs.fs.size[<path>|*,pused|pfree], vfs.fs.inode[<path>|*,pfree], system.swap.size[,pused], system.cpu.load[percpu,avg15], system.pressure[memory,full], service.failed[<pattern>], proc.num[<name>], docker.containers[unhealthy|restarting|running|stopped|all], agent.ping, system.uptime, clock.synchronized. Macros are allowed in the parameters.
- `name` (String)
- `threshold` (String) A number or a macro, e.g. "90" or "{$DISK_CRIT}".

Optional:

- `breaches_to_fire` (Number)
- `clears_to_resolve` (Number)
- `defer_to_builtin` (String) A built-in alert this rule duplicates (cpu_high, memory_high, disk_full, mount_full, inodes_low, swap_in_use, service_failed, clock_unsynced, device_unreachable): while that alert is on for a device, the rule doesn't notify a second time.
- `description` (String)
- `enabled` (Boolean)
- `func` (String)
- `severity` (String) "warning" (summary email) or "critical" (sent right away).
- `window_minutes` (Number)
